title: Affine-basis lower-tail truncation transition
statement: Let X be a scheme, V an affine open, F an integer-indexed complex of O_X-modules, and assume every homology sheaf of F has zero positive cohomology on every affine W contained in V. Put E = tau_{<a}(QF), and G = evaluation on V followed by exact forgetting to abelian groups. For all integers a,i,n with 1-i <= n, H^i(RG(tau_{>=-n}E)) -> H^i(RG(tau_{>=-n+1}E)), induced by the canonical truncation transition, is an isomorphism. Derived-category universes are arbitrary.

source.place: Tag 08D4, proof of (2), using the acyclicity assumption instead of quasi-coherence; cohomology.tex Tag 0BKT

proof.text: For any module M and natural q, use the open-restriction module-cohomology isomorphism at V, then the module-cohomology-source comparison on V.toScheme. If H^(q+1)(V,M|V) is subsingleton, the additive equivalence makes the module cohomology subsingleton; exact scalar forgetting gives a zero abelian object, and the open-restriction isomorphism transports zero to (G.rightDerived (q+1)).obj M. This is the proved private helper evaluation_rightDerived_isZero.

Put M=H^(-n)(tau_<a QF). If -n<a, the homology map of truncLT inclusion is invertible; compose its associated isomorphism with homologyFunctorFactors to identify M with F.homology (-n). Apply the preceding helper to hhomology at W=V, and transport along rightDerived applied to this isomorphism. Otherwise the t-structure support bound makes M zero, and the additive right derived functor preserves zero. Thus (G.rightDerived (q+1)).obj M is zero for every natural q.

For j with n+j>=1 let q=(n+j).toNat-1. Integer arithmetic gives n+j=q+1. The singleFunctorIsoCompQ, commShiftIso of the unbounded right derived functor, homology shiftIso, and homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso identify degree-j homology of RG(Q(M[0])[n]) with R^(q+1)G(M). The latter is zero by the preceding calculation. This applies to j=i and j=i+1 because n>=1-i.

Obtain the distinguished lower-truncation step triangle of E at n, whose middle arrow is exactly natTransTruncGEOfLE (-n) (-n+1). Map it through the triangulated functor G.rightDerivedFunctor. Its first-object homology vanishes in degrees i and i+1 by the previous step. Apply DerivedCategory.isIso_homologyMap_mor₂, the monic-and-epic consequence of the long exact homology sequence, to obtain the displayed isomorphism.

theorem affineBasisLowerTail_sections_step_isIso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (V : X.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wC} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (F : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hhomology : ∀ (W : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → W ≤ V → ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((F.homology n).restrict W.ι).H (q + 1)))
    (a i n : ℤ) (hn : 1 - i ≤ n) :
    let S := SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (op V)
    letI : S.Additive := inferInstanceAs
      ((SheafOfModules.forget.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj (op V)).Additive)
    let G := S ⋙ forget₂
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op V))) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
    let t := DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    let E := (t.truncLT a).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F)
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).map
      (G.rightDerivedFunctor.map ((t.natTransTruncGEOfLE
        (-n) (-n + 1) (Int.le_add_one (le_refl (-n)))).app E)))
